page: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per virtual core. Local persistent storage is bundled with a 480 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark testing demonstrates solid compute and memory capability. In synthetic stress tests, single-core stress-ng performance reached 3,208.88 points, positioning in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng achieved 74,749.71 points, placing in the top 25%. Geekbench evaluation shows a single-core score of 1,746.0 and a multi-core score of 14,468.0, with strong results in image processing at 14,143.0 points. Memory subsystems recorded a strong PassMark memory score of 2,891.74 and uncached large-block read throughput of 126.87 GB/sec. For lightweight artificial intelligence workloads, text generation throughput using a 135M parameter language model reached 342.31 tokens per second.

The CPU flags feature support for AES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2 instructions, although advanced AVX-512 extensions and AMX tiles are not enabled. This hardware baseline yields solid throughput for general concurrency rather than matrix-heavy vectorized calculations. Operating costs are distributed across dedicated core density, balanced system memory, and direct NVMe storage, making it cost-efficient for predictable sustained loads requiring consistent dedicated CPU execution.

Given its 1:4 resource ratio, dedicated core tenancy, and integrated NVMe capacity, Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is well-matched for mid-sized relational database servers, backend application microservices, caching layers like Redis, static web serving clusters, and distributed build pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for balanced, dedicated multi-core workloads. Powered by AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 96 GB of system RAM, and a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD. It features a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements highlight top-tier single-core stress-ng throughput of 3,208.88 points and strong multi-core execution of 74,749.71 points, backed by 2,891.74 points on the PassMark memory benchmark. CPU instruction sets include AES, SHA-NI, and AVX, but exclude AVX-512 and matrix extensions. With stable dedicated resource allocation and high NVMe transfer rates, the instance delivers predictable cost efficiency for continuous workloads, including relational database engines, Redis caching tiers, application backends, and multi-threaded continuous integration compilation jobs.
